thread.title: PHOTOS: Bison roam Custer State Park ahead of 60th Buffalo Roundup

author: MIKE BROWNLEE Journal staff
title: PHOTOS: Bison roam Custer State Park ahead of 60th Buffalo Roundup
text:
Alert Top Story PHOTOS: Bison roam Custer State Park ahead of 60th Buffalo Roundup Mike Brownlee Sep 24, 2025 3 hrs ago 0 A tour of the buffalo at Custer State Park ahead of Friday's Buffalo Roundup. "Custer State Park can only handle so many animals year-round," Austin said. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee, Journal staff A pair of bison runs through a field at Custer State Park. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Jason Gooder, operations manager at Custer State Park, discusses the roundup map with media and others during a tour of the Custer State Park grounds on Wednesday, Sept. 24. Mike Brownlee Journal staff A buffalo rests in the tall grass at Custer State Park. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff A group of buffalo walk along a Custer State Park road on Wednesday, Sept. 24. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff "We round up the herd and bring them down to the corral system for their annual vaccinations, health checkup, and then we'll cull off a number of animals to keep the herd at (manageable) levels for the winter," said Lydia Austin with Custer State Park. Some buffaloes will be sold at auction. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff A buffalo walks in a field at Custer State Park on Wednesday, Sept. 24. Hundreds of people at the park and in the area are gearing up for the 60th annual Governor's Buffalo Roundup, set for Friday, Sept. 26. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Custer State Park started its buffalo herd with 36 bison in 1914, according to Austin. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff The fall colors are vibrant at Custer State Park. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff Mike Brownlee Journal staff To help with such a big event, the park will also bring in 10 support staff from the South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks division, as well as law enforcement and conservation officers. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Friday, Sept. 26 marks the 60th annual Governor's Buffalo Roundup, where staff and volunteers will round up an expected 1,400 bison, taking them down through the hills to holding pens at Custer State Park. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff A buffalo grazes at Custer State Park on Wednesday, Sept. 24. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Buffalo block traffic at Custer State Park on Wednesday, Sept. 24. The Buffalo Roundup starts 9:30 a.m. on Friday, Sept 26, with parking lots opening at 6:15 a.m. Park officials recommend visitors arrive early due to how busy the event gets. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff A buffalo mother and her calf at Custer State Park on Wednesday, Sept. 24. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Sixty skilled horseback riders will be rounding up the bison. Mike Brownlee, Journal staff Jason Gooder, operations manager at Custer State Park, said, "Typically, we see around 20,000 plus, (people) this being the 60th, and the media push that out there, we're expecting maybe 30,000 or more." Mike Brownlee, Journal staff A bison stands in front of the Custer State Park Bison Center sign on Wednesday, Sept. 24.
